children: Paramount Skydance (PSKY, Financials) is edging closer to the conclusion of its planned $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery following a compromise with 12 U.S. states and the Writers Guild of America.
The deal clears a major legal hurdle and opens the way for the firms to move toward a closure, but final judicial approval and other conditions have to be met.

I expect this transaction to close in approximately two weeks, said David Ellison, CEO, in an email to workers. The timeline may matter to Paramount because the merger agreement says it must pay WBD shareholders nearly $7 million a day if the acquisition doesnt close by Sept. 30.

A lengthy delay may send those ticking fees as high as $1.7 billion, further costing the acquisition. Closing sooner would minimize that expense and give Paramount a jump on merging Warner Bros. Discovery assets.
The merger would see Paramounts studios and streaming business join forces with key WBD assets like HBO Max and CNN to create a much larger media portfolio.
For investors the question is not so much whether the merger can be done, but how fast the businesses can close it and whether the merged business can provide the projected benefits.
The next catalyst is final regulatory and court approval and the closure of the acquisition thereafter.

title: Paramount Just Cleared a Major Hurdle for Its $110B Warner Bros. Deal
